title: Paul's Voyage to Rome, Shipwreck

questions.question: Paul was put in the charge of a centurion of the Augustan Cohort named what?
options: Julius
Cornelius
Claudius
Marcus
questions.explanation: Acts 27:1 (ESV): "And when it was decided that we should sail for Italy, they delivered Paul and some other prisoners to a centurion of the Augustan Cohort named Julius."

questions.question: Paul warned that the voyage would be with injury and much loss, but the centurion paid more attention to whom than to Paul?
options: The pilot and the owner of the ship
The majority of the passengers on board
The harbor master at Fair Havens
The Roman officers in his escort
questions.correctAnswer: The pilot and the owner of the ship
questions.explanation: Acts 27:11 (ESV): "But the centurion paid more attention to the pilot and to the owner of the ship than to what Paul said."

questions.question: A violent storm called the Northeaster struck the ship. What was thrown overboard to lighten the ship on the third day?
options: The ship's tackle (equipment)
Wheat from the cargo hold
The ship's boats and ropes
Passengers' personal baggage
questions.explanation: Acts 27:19 (ESV): "And on the third day they threw the ship's tackle overboard with their own hands."

questions.question: An angel of God stood by Paul during the night and told him what?
options: "Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before Caesar. And behold, God has granted you all those who sail with you."
"Paul, the Lord will keep you through this storm for his purposes."
"Fear not, for God has heard your prayer and will calm the sea."
"I am sent to protect you; no one on this ship shall perish."
questions.correctAnswer: "Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before Caesar. And behold, God has granted you all those who sail with you."
questions.explanation: Acts 27:24 (ESV): "Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before Caesar. And behold, God has granted you all those who sail with you."

questions.question: Paul urged everyone to take food, saying in 14 days they had not eaten. He took bread, gave thanks to God, broke it, and began to eat. How many were on the ship?
options: 276 persons
216 persons
136 persons
316 persons
questions.explanation: Acts 27:37-38 (ESV): "(We were in all 276 persons in the ship.) And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, throwing out the wheat into the sea."

questions.question: As the ship was about to run aground, the sailors tried to escape using the ship's boat. What did Paul tell the centurion and soldiers?
options: "Unless these men stay in the ship, you cannot be saved."
"If the sailors abandon ship, we will all perish in the sea."
"God has promised our safety but only if we stay together."
"Stop them, for their leaving will doom us all to destruction."
questions.correctAnswer: "Unless these men stay in the ship, you cannot be saved."
questions.explanation: Acts 27:31 (ESV): "Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, 'Unless these men stay in the ship, you cannot be saved.'"

questions.question: When the ship ran aground, what did the soldiers plan to do with the prisoners?
options: Kill them so that none could swim away and escape
Bind them together so they could not scatter in the water
Leave them on the ship while soldiers swam ashore first
Transfer them to the ship's boat for safe passage
questions.correctAnswer: Kill them so that none could swim away and escape
questions.explanation: Acts 27:42 (ESV): "The soldiers' plan was to kill the prisoners, lest any should swim away and escape."

questions.question: How did all 276 persons get safely to land?
options: Some swam; others used planks and other pieces from the ship
The sea became calm and they were able to wade ashore
The ship drifted close enough for all to step off safely
Small fishing boats from the island came out to rescue them
questions.correctAnswer: Some swam; others used planks and other pieces from the ship
questions.explanation: Acts 27:44 (ESV): "And the rest on planks or on pieces of the ship. And so it was that all were brought safely to land."

questions.question: The centurion Julius showed Paul kindness by allowing him to visit friends at Sidon during a port stop. What did he allow Paul's friends to do?
options: Provide for Paul's needs (be cared for by them)
Bring him money and supplies for the voyage
Come aboard and speak with Paul on the ship
Accompany Paul for the remainder of the journey
questions.correctAnswer: Provide for Paul's needs (be cared for by them)
questions.explanation: Acts 27:3 (ESV): "The next day we put in at Sidon. And Julius treated Paul kindly and gave him leave to go to his friends and be cared for."

questions.question: Paul reassured those on the ship by saying: "Take heart, for I believe God that it will be exactly as I have been told." What else did he add would happen?
options: They must run aground on some island, but not one of them would lose their life
They would find a harbor where they could wait safely until the storm passed
God had promised him calm waters would come before they reached Malta
He trusted God to calm the Northeaster before the ship broke apart
questions.correctAnswer: They must run aground on some island, but not one of them would lose their life
questions.explanation: Acts 27:25-26 (ESV): "So take heart, men, for I have faith in God that it will be exactly as I have been told. But we must run aground on some island."

questions.question: What harbor were they trying to reach when they left Fair Havens (since it was unsuitable for wintering)?
options: Phoenix
Rhegium
Puteoli
Syracuse
questions.explanation: Acts 27:12 (ESV): "...the majority decided to put out to sea from there, on the chance that somehow they could reach Phoenix, a harbor of Crete, facing both southwest and northwest, and spend the winter there."

questions.question: When the soldiers planned to kill the prisoners, who stopped them?
options: The centurion Julius, wishing to save Paul
Paul himself who warned them of God's judgment
The ship's captain who had authority over all on board
God who struck the soldiers with sudden fear
questions.correctAnswer: The centurion Julius, wishing to save Paul
questions.explanation: Acts 27:43 (ESV): "But the centurion, wishing to save Paul, kept them from carrying out their plan."

questions.question: Paul had warned before the voyage set out that sailing would result in injury and loss. He had specifically said they should stay at which harbor?
options: Fair Havens
Phoenix
Cnidus
Myra
questions.explanation: Acts 27:8-10 (ESV): "...we came to a place called Fair Havens... Paul advised them, saying, 'Men, I perceive that the voyage will be with injury and much loss...'..."

questions.question: After the ship ran aground and the bow was stuck, the stern began to break apart. What cargo had previously been thrown overboard to keep the ship light?
options: The wheat
The ship's tackle
The anchors
Passengers' baggage
questions.explanation: Acts 27:38 (ESV): "And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, throwing out the wheat into the sea."

questions.question: Paul took bread, gave thanks to God before all, and broke it. This caused the spirits of those aboard to do what?
options: They were all encouraged and themselves ate food
They were convinced Paul was a prophet of God
They praised God and prayed with Paul for safety
They stopped their plans to escape and stayed calm
questions.correctAnswer: They were all encouraged and themselves ate food
questions.explanation: Acts 27:36 (ESV): "Then they were all encouraged and ate some food themselves."

key_verse_text: "So take heart, men, for I have faith in God that it will be exactly as I have been told."
